sentence_of_record: CONTENT-DISJOINT-SPLIT-AUDIT (2026-09-23, zero calls; data steward, independently recomputed): the pools of record are id-disjoint but not content-disjoint. On the union pool paeec37aa28063c75, 471 EVAL ids (427 distinct texts) have an exact-text TRAIN twin and 478 have one under norm-v1: GPQA 288 (382 pairs, all with the same options and answer, 367 with the options shuffled), MMLU-Pro 185 (68 true duplicates at 0.999 correctness agreement, 127 stem-only variants at 0.753), MATH 3, BBH 2. On the MMLU-Pro pool of record p2dca21ab5f4ef3ae, 37 exact / 70 norm-v1 judgeable ids have a TRAIN twin, every one an unlinked sentinel row. Keyed on the question actually judged, 64 share the option set and 31 are full ordered duplicates. Of the incident's 1,020 CLEAN questions, 12 exact / 23 norm-v1 were frozen-tree members. 20NG (by its ingest's dedup rule), BFCL and Multi-SWE (repo-family closure; no content key) have no cross-side twins. The engine's stem-key closure (since 13f2142) moves 171 rows on p2dca (3,770 / 8,230, the af_clean_s42 split); the SPLIT-FUNCTION-IMPL figure 3,537 is not reproduced by any reading of the data.

plain_description.what: An audit of whether the training and evaluation pools share questions with the same text, not only different IDs. It covers the union pool, the MMLU-Pro pool of record, 20 Newsgroups, BFCL and Multi-SWE. No calls.
plain_description.why: If evaluation questions have text twins on the training side, tree-building and rubric writing may have seen them, which would weaken evaluation claims.
plain_description.information: Zero twins would make the splits clean. Twins would need to be disclosed, or the data rebuilt. Result: done (descriptive). The pools are ID-disjoint but not content-disjoint. 471 union evaluation IDs have an exact-text training twin, mostly GPQA and MMLU-Pro. On the MMLU-Pro pool of record, 37 exact (70 normalised) have one, and 31 judged questions are full copies. 20 Newsgroups, BFCL and Multi-SWE have no cross-side twins. The effect on any readout is not measured.
